Predicates:
GetsMonkeypox(x) ::: x gets Monkeypox.
VirusIn(x, y) ::: virus y occurs in x.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Symptoms(x, y) ::: y is a symptom of x.
FeelsTired(x) ::: x feels tired.
Fever(x) ::: x has fever.
Headache(x) ::: x has headache.
MusclePains(x) ::: x has muscle pains.
Tiredness(x) ::: x feels tired.
GetsFlu(x) ::: x gets the flu.
SymptomOf(x, y) ::: y is a symptom of x.
OccursIn(y, x) ::: y occurs in x.
Premises:
∀x (VirusIn(x, MonkeypoxVirus) → GetsMonkeypox(x)) ::: When Monkeypox virus occurs in a being, it may get Monkeypox.
∀x (VirusIn(x, y) → Animal(x)) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals.
Human(Human) ::: humans are mammals.
Mammal(x) → Animal(x) ::: Mammals are animals.
Symptoms(Monkeypox, fever) ∧ Symptoms(Monkeypox, headache) ∧ Symptoms(Monkeypox, musclePains) ∧ Symptoms(Monkeypox, tiredness) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, and tiredness.
FeelsTired(x) → GetsFlu(x) ::: People feel tired when they get the flu.
Conclusion:
¬∃x (GetsFlu(x)) ::: No one gets the flu.
